summary: The most important signals this week are an authoritative benchmark and a procurement move. On 12 November the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) released World Fusion Outlook 2026 in Vienna, citing record private fusion financing of about $4.5 billion in the 12 months to July 2026 and more than $14 billion since 2021. The same day, the UK STEP programme launched procurement of five major systems, worth up to £115 million. On the quantum-energy side, China Southern Power Grid issued a public tender for "power-market clearing simulation research based on quantum computing" (a ceiling of 2.775 million yuan, with explicit validation on photonic quantum hardware); Germany's BMFTR is funding the QUANDA project at about €4 million, using trapped-ion quantum computing for energy anomaly detection; and a peer-reviewed Scientific Reports paper shows that a hybrid quantum algorithm did not beat random sampling on grid-optimisation cases of 5–13 generating units (in simulation), while a 17-qubit live-hardware power-flow demonstration at TU Delft also illustrated limits of scale and noise. On the RWA side, the European Central Bank, the European Commission and ESMA issued a public call for members of a European Tokenisation Standards Group (ETSG), closing on 27 November; Hong Kong's EX.IO and ZoneLink signed an agreement to advance RWAs of Japanese solar plants and data centres.
trends: Quantum × the grid: buyer-side procurement (China Southern Power Grid's 2.775 million yuan tender; Germany's QUANDA at about €4 million) appeared in the same week as academic calibration (Scientific Reports found no advantage over random sampling on cases of 5–13 units; a 6-qubit circuit at TU Delft reached a depth of 165 layers), a sign that the field is moving from demonstration publicity to a stage with budgets and benchmarks.

Fusion capital: IAEA, citing FIA data, reports about $4.5 billion of private fusion financing in the 12 months to July 2026 and more than $14 billion cumulatively; the UK STEP programme has launched procurement of up to £115 million in one go, and funds are starting to flow to supply-chain segments such as blankets, the fuel cycle and control systems.

Regulatory divergence: the EU, through the ECB, the Commission and ESMA, is pushing for common tokenisation standards (ETSG closes on 27 November). In China, TokenPost reported on 8 November that a financial-work report submitted by the State Council to the NPC Standing Committee on 3 November listed measures including "strengthening supervision of RWA tokenisation", but gave no specific new rules.

Green tokenisation in Hong Kong: according to a 9 November summary of FinTech Week by the Hong Kong Green Finance Association, Hong Kong Exchanges is deploying a multi-asset tokenisation platform for carbon credits and running a pilot in trading of renewable energy certificates.

Risk notice: a GlobeNewswire press release on 11 November promoted a USPR token billed as "US electricity-equity tokenisation", priced at under 1 US cent and emphasising a 30 November "milestone", with language stressing early-mover gains and no disclosure of underlying assets or regulatory information. It is a typical promotional "energy RWA" and should be strictly distinguished from licensed, compliant projects.
footer: All facts and figures in this brief are taken from the public sources listed. The China Southern Power Grid project is at the tender stage and has not yet been awarded; QUANDA is a research award with no performance results yet; EX.IO × ZoneLink is a cooperation framework with no disclosed issue size; the Scientific Reports results are ideal-hardware simulations; USPR is mentioned only as a risk notice and is not an assessment or a recommendation. Time window: 2026-11-06 to 2026-11-13 (Zurich time).

items.title: IAEA releases World Fusion Outlook 2026: private fusion annual financing hits a record of about $4.5 billion, and the industry enters a "critical transition"
items.what: On 12 November the International Atomic Energy Agency released the fourth edition of World Fusion Outlook 2026 (128 pages, 100 figures) during the third meeting of the World Fusion Energy Group at its Vienna headquarters. According to the Fusion Industry Association (FIA) and NucNet, the report cites FIA's 2026 industry survey: private fusion companies raised a record of about $4.5 billion in the 12 months to July 2026, and more than $14 billion cumulatively since 2021. The report says fusion is in a "critical transition" whose next stage depends on the ability to integrate science, engineering, investment, regulation and international cooperation, and it includes a special discussion of the data foundations needed for AI to be used in fusion research. The IAEA press-release headline also refers to an "$80 billion financing challenge" and future deployment scenarios.
items.why: This is one of the most authoritative annual benchmarks in global fusion, and it offers a common yardstick for investment scale and deployment progress in public statements. It also cautions that a planned plant is not the same as electricity generated, and that regulation, supply chains and data integration — not capital alone — are the bottlenecks.

items.title: UK STEP launches procurement of five major systems, worth up to £115 million; First Light partners with the Central Laser Facility on fast ignition
items.what: According to the American Nuclear Society (ANS) on 12 November, UK Fusion Energy (UKFE), the UK Atomic Energy Authority unit responsible for the spherical-tokamak energy prototype plant STEP, launched a procurement programme seeking industrial partners in five areas, with a combined budget of up to £115 million (about $152 million) and two-year contracts: a breeding-blanket system, a fuel-cycle system, a plant control system, and support for a technology test facility and for systems engineering / overall integration. At the same time, Oxford's First Light Fusion is working with the Central Laser Facility (CLF) of the UK Science and Technology Facilities Council on high-energy electron generation and energy deposition in the second step of its FLARE inertial-fusion scheme — fast ignition of high-density fuel with a high-intensity laser.
items.why: A government programme moving from research grants to engineering procurement means that supply-chain segments such as blankets, the fuel cycle and control systems are beginning to have clear orders and contract periods — one of the most verifiable signals of fusion industrialisation.

items.title: China Southern Power Grid tenders "power-market clearing simulation research based on quantum computing": ceiling 2.775 million yuan, with validation required on photonic quantum hardware
items.what: On 6 November, China Southern Power Grid's unified supply-chain service platform published a tender notice from the Southern Control Centre for "power-market clearing simulation research based on quantum computing" (procurement number CG0000022002411480). Funding is in place, the maximum bid price is 2.775 million yuan, and the service period runs to 31 December 2027. The research covers: a framework combining quantum and classical computing (constraint handling, spatiotemporal decomposition, hybrid optimisation); a hybrid quantum-classical algorithm suited to the hardware topology of a photonic quantum computer; and a closed-loop experimental validation on an actual photonic quantum computer. Deliverables include one research report, one set of algorithm software, three papers in core or SCI/EI journals, and six invention-patent applications accepted for examination. The bid deadline and opening are at 09:00 on 27 November.
items.why: This is a grid company procuring quantum power-optimisation research through a public tender with a clear budget and deliverables, a better indication of real buyer commitment than demonstration news. The notice itself also acknowledges that NISQ devices are limited by qubit numbers and coherence times, and that the aim is "forward-looking technical reserve".
items.src: China Southern Power Grid unified supply-chain service platform

items.title: Germany's QUANDA project starts: about €4 million, trapped-ion quantum computing connected to a supercomputer, testing energy anomaly detection
items.what: On 12 November, German trapped-ion quantum-computing company QUDORA and partners announced the start of the three-year QUANDA (Quantum Anomaly Detection & Analysis) project, funded under the "Development of Digital Technologies" programme of the Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space (BMFTR). The award-certificate ceremony was held in Berlin on 9 November; partner GWDG said funding was about €4 million. The project will integrate QUDORA's trapped-ion quantum computer into a high-performance computing environment, develop an automated hybrid pipeline covering job submission, compilation and execution, and test quantum machine-learning anomaly detection in three real energy settings (for example unusual electricity use, changes in equipment-sensor readings, and generation and distribution anomalies). The consortium is led by Deggendorf Institute of Technology and includes six organisations such as Leibniz University Hannover, GWDG, UBT Future Energy Lab Wunsiedel and ZENOB.
items.why: The project puts quantum computing into a real workflow of "HPC + energy operations data", rather than isolated test cases. It is still only a research award, however, with no evidence yet of outperforming classical methods — a point QubitWire also makes explicitly.

items.title: A "reality check" on quantum algorithms for the grid: a Scientific Reports benchmark finds no advantage over random sampling; a 17-qubit live power-flow demonstration at TU Delft exposes a depth bottleneck
items.what: On 11 November, a University of Tennessee at Chattanooga team (funded by TVA and NIST) published an open-access paper in Scientific Reports, the first direct evaluation of hybrid quantum-classical variational algorithms for a single-period AC-OPF-UC problem with unit commitment and a full AC power flow. A fully discretised QAOA scheme needed too many qubits even on small cases. A scheme that encoded only unit commitment on the quantum side did not beat uniform random sampling on random cases of 5–13 units (ideal-hardware simulation); the authors think a scale of 24 units or more would be needed before any advantage could be judged. On 12 November, TU Delft reported that researcher Zeynab Kaseb had for the first time connected the DelftBlue supercomputer and Quantum Inspire in a workflow, using QAOA on QuTech's 17-qubit Tuna-17 processor to compute a two-node power flow: a 4-qubit version found the optimum 215 times (about 21%); a 6-qubit version had a lower residual (0.003262 versus 0.01053), but circuit depth rose from 30 layers to 165, and the optimum appeared only 16 times (1.56%), close to random-sampling level.
items.why: These two results offer a peer-reviewed and live-hardware counterpoint to claims of "quantum optimisation of the grid": the workflow can be run, but at current scale there is no demonstrable advantage.

items.title: The ECB, the European Commission and ESMA call for members of a European Tokenisation Standards Group (ETSG), closing on 27 November
items.what: On 9 November, the European Commission's Directorate-General for Financial Stability, Financial Services and Capital Markets Union announced that the European Central Bank, together with the Commission and the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), was inviting wholesale-finance stakeholders to apply to join the European Tokenisation Standards Group (ETSG), to develop common standards for an interoperable tokenised financial ecosystem and a compliance-monitoring framework, and to advise EU authorities on how to encourage adherence to the standards. The group will be chaired by industry, with the three public institutions as observers, and is open to EU associations, private institutions, global institutions, fintech firms and DLT technology providers. The background is a December 2025 market-integration and supervision package (MISP) requiring post-trade institutions to advance interoperability of DLT infrastructure.
items.why: EU tokenisation is moving from "pilot exemptions" toward common technical standards. Future energy and green-asset tokenisation issued or settled in the EU will likely need to connect to these standards.

items.title: EX.IO and ZoneLink sign an agreement to advance RWAs of Japanese solar plants and data-centre assets
items.what: On 6 November, EX.IO Group announced in Hong Kong a cooperation agreement with ZoneLink Technology, which focuses on "AI × renewable energy and digital assets", initially targeting tokenisation of Japanese solar plants and IDC data centres. The two sides will assess cash flows from solar power sales and from data-centre leasing, hosting and computing-power services; the specific underlying assets, issuance arrangements and revenue-sharing mechanism will depend on due diligence and applicable law and regulation. ZoneLink is responsible for asset screening and document coordination; EX.IO for product structure, tokenisation, issuance coordination and distribution. The announcement says Japan's FIT/FIP schemes and long-term corporate power-purchase agreements (PPAs) can provide relatively stable cash flows.
items.why: Bundling "green power + computing power" has become a new narrative for energy RWAs: demand for electricity from AI data centres links renewable-energy cash flows with computing-lease revenues. This is still only a cooperation framework, however, with no specific issue size.
